reconstructed_theorem_text: For arbitrary natural numbers d,n, a real number kappa, and every family O of real orthogonal n by n matrices indexed by Fin(d div n), the displayed expression returns the following real d by d matrix. Put q = d div n and r = d mod n, with natural-number division and remainder, so d = q*n + r. For each j in {0,...,q-1}, define the real n by n block B_j = ((kappa+1)/2) I_n - ((kappa-1)/4)(O_j + O_j^T). The resulting real d by d matrix A has q consecutive blocks B_0,...,B_(q-1), followed by I_r, and all entries between distinct blocks or between a main block and the tail are zero. The pair (i,j), with inner coordinate i in {0,...,n-1} and block index j in {0,...,q-1}, maps to coordinate j*n+i. Tail coordinate k in {0,...,r-1} maps to q*n+k. Both row and column indices use this same map (reindexing uses its inverse to retrieve the original entries). If r=0, the tail is empty: I_0 has no entries and adds no coordinates. No positivity, dimension lower bound, spectral bound, or assertion about this matrix is part of this expression. Natural division is used even for n=0: then q=0 and r=d, so the expression returns I_d.
objects: Natural numbers d,n; real scalar kappa; q=d div n; r=d mod n; an indexed family O_j of real orthogonal n by n matrices; blocks B_j; the reindexed real matrix A; identity matrices I_n and I_r; the coordinate equivalence e from ((Fin n x Fin q) disjoint-union Fin r) to Fin d.
domains: d,n belong to the natural numbers, including zero where not otherwise restricted; kappa belongs to the real numbers; j belongs to Fin q; inner coordinates belong to Fin n; residual coordinates belong to Fin r; A has rows and columns in Fin d and real entries; O maps Fin q to the real orthogonal group on Fin n.
quantifiers: This is a function expression with implicit parameters d,n : natural numbers and explicit inputs kappa : real and O : Fin(d div n) -> orthogonalGroup(Fin n, real). It defines an output for every such input; it is not a universally quantified proposition asserting a matrix property.
assumptions: Only the input types are imposed: O_j is orthogonal for each j. There is no assumption 3<=n, n<=d, 4<=kappa, or n>0.
conclusion: The value is the real d by d matrix A described in the reconstructed text: diag(B_0,...,B_(q-1),I_r) in exactly the specified finite coordinate order.
scopes: The matrix blocks are ordered by j first and inner coordinate i second: global coordinate j*n+i; the residual tail starts at q*n. The coordinate equivalence is used for both rows and columns. An empty residual set contributes no identity coordinates. The local equivalence e is used only to define the output matrix. At n=0 there are no main blocks and the whole matrix is I_d; d=0 yields an empty matrix.
constant_dependencies: The block coefficients are exactly (kappa+1)/2 and (kappa-1)/4. The tail coefficient is exactly 1. q and r depend on d,n. Every B_j depends on kappa and O_j, and its size depends on n. No existential constants or hidden restrictions occur.
